title: The lib owns the record-domain laws; commands render
rationale: The lib is fabro natively embedded (README product posture): an embedder must validate records and classify staleness without shelling out. Pre-C1 both laws lived as pub(crate) CLI modules with an inverted dependency (full_verdict called up into commands::hint_fields) - five CLI consumers, zero embedder reach. Byte-neutral move, proven by the differential battery.

description: jiff Span constructors PANIC on out-of-range fields: Span::new().hours(n) panics for |n| > 175,307,616 (jiff-0.2 span.rs range check) — so saturating an i64 day count into Span::hours() trades an overflow panic for a RANGE panic, and Timestamp + Span panics on out-of-range results (the checked_add variant returns Result). Sprint-21 standards-review blocker: StaleRule::verdict computed (days + 1) * 24 as Span::hours for a shelf that could saturate at i64::MAX (absurd config) — debug panic, release wrap to 0 hours → EVERY record Stale (verdict inversion). RULE: timestamp math over possibly-huge values belongs in plain i64 seconds/milliseconds (now.as_millisecond() - recorded.as_millisecond(), saturating the boundary) — exact, overflow-proof, and byte-identical to the reference's Math.floor millisecond semantics. Reserve jiff Span arithmetic for values known to be small.
resolution: Compare timestamps in plain i64 milliseconds (now.as_millisecond() - recorded.as_millisecond() >= (days+1).saturating_mul(86_400_000)) — exact and overflow-proof; Timestamp::checked_add returns Result for the Span path, but avoid the Span construction entirely for possibly-huge values. Pinned by a saturation unit test (i64::MAX days -> Fresh).

description: serde_json with preserve_order: Map::remove does NOT preserve key order — it swaps the LAST key into the freed slot (Vec semantics). Deleting a mid-object key (e.g. the legacy `outcome` field during a rewrite) silently promotes the last key (often `id`) into that position, diverging from JS `delete`/spread order. Use Map::shift_remove for order-preserving deletion. Found as a latent parity bug in mulch sprint 22 (battery fixtures had the key last, so the reorder was invisible until a mid-object fixture landed); fixed in normalize + migrate with the mid-object battery pin.
resolution: Use Map::shift_remove for order-preserving deletion (landed in normalize_legacy_outcome + migrate_legacy_line, mid-object battery pin added); grep for plain .remove( on mid-object key deletions in serde preserve_order codebases.

description: serde_json with the preserve_order feature: Map::remove has SWAP semantics (the last entry moves into the removed key's slot), not shift semantics - any rewrite that must keep sibling key order needs shift_remove (mulch doctor repair passes, sprint 24; migrate_legacy_line in records.rs already used shift_remove for the same reason). grep shift_remove before deleting keys from a parsed JSON object.
resolution: use shift_remove whenever sibling key order must survive a delete from a parsed JSON object; the differential battery caught the silent reorder (sprint 24 anchors fix moved recorded_at two slots early) and the fix is pinned by unit + battery tests

name: clap-rejects-empty-pathbuf-args-accepts-empty-strings
description: Verified in a scratch repo (clap 4.6.7, sprint 25): Option<PathBuf> args reject '--flag ' at parse time ('a value is required for ... but none was supplied', ErrorKind::empty_value from PathBufValueParser) while Option<String> args accept the empty value. Consequence for parity surfaces: a JS-truthiness gate on an argv flag ('--batch ' = no batch) needs a String arg, not PathBuf — the empty value must reach command code to be dropped there (mulch cli.rs batch, mulch-1209).

name: rust-line-continuation-eats-indent
description: A Rust string continuation (backslash at line end) SWALLOWS the next line's leading whitespace — multi-line literals lose their indentation, so YAML/JSON children in test fixtures must stay on ONE source line (or be built with concat!/format!). Hit twice in sprint 32 fixtures. Came out of HANDOFF's 'Known ephemera' (file removed 2026-10-17 — ephemera now live as records, not in a handoff file).
